S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S056.name: Excessive_Anxiety_Worry
S056.description: Excessive anxiety and worry (expectant apprehension) occurring persistently about a number of events or activities.

subtypes.Chronic Worry: Worry occurs more days than not for at least 6 months.
subtypes.Generalized Worry: Worry is not confined to specific topics but spreads to various domains like work, school, family, and finances.
subtypes.Catastrophizing: Jumping to conclusions that minor mistakes or events will lead to irreversible disasters.
subtypes.Intolerance of Uncertainty: Unable to tolerate future uncertainty, trapped in 'what if' questions.

S057.name: Uncontrollable_Worry
S057.description: The subjective experience of finding it difficult to stop or control the worry.

subtypes.Failure to Control: Unable to regulate worry despite efforts to stop or distract oneself.
subtypes.Intrusive Worry: Worries suddenly intrude into the mind and interfere with focus while doing other tasks.
subtypes.Chaining of Worry: One worry triggers another in a chain reaction, escalating to catastrophic thoughts.

S058.name: Restlessness_Tension
S058.description: Restlessness, or feeling keyed up or on edge.

subtypes.Feeling Keyed Up: Feeling anxious and wound up like a spring, unable to stay still.
subtypes.Physical Tension: The entire body feels stiff and tense, unable to relax.
subtypes.Nervousness: Nerves are on edge, being startled easily by minor sounds or stimuli.

S060.name: Irritability
S060.description: A state of reacting sensitively or sharply to minor stimuli.

subtypes.Low Frustration Tolerance: Getting annoyed immediately at trivial stimuli that would normally be ignored.
subtypes.Snappiness: Nerves are sharp, leading to sensitive and aggressive reactions to small matters.
subtypes.Exhausted Patience: Patience is depleted, making it impossible to endure minor inconveniences or delays.

symptom.disease_info: Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD) is characterized by persistent, excessive, and difficult-to-control worry about multiple domains of life, occurring more days than not for at least six months and associated with physical and cognitive manifestations such as tension, fatigue, concentration problems, and disturbed sleep. Clinically, patients often describe a longstanding tendency to "overthink" that has escalated in intensity and begun to interfere with social, academic, or occupational functioning. The course is typically chronic and fluctuating, with symptoms waxing during periods of stress and only partially remitting between episodes. It is distinguished from other anxiety disorders by the breadth and shifting nature of worries, rather than focus on specific triggers as in phobias or discrete attacks as in panic disorder, and from mood disorders by the primary experience of apprehensive expectation rather than pervasive low mood.

patient.personality: Brenda is a driven, competitive young woman who channels her energy into science, leadership, and extracurriculars while holding herself to very high standards.
patient.stressor: Brenda’s anxiety began to escalate in the second year of her bachelor’s program, when she simultaneously took on an overloaded course schedule, a demanding lab assistant role, and leadership in a STEM outreach group in hopes of building a standout profile for competitive biotech internships. Initially she thrived on the pace, but a series of minor lab setbacks, a rejected grant application, and tension with a senior student she didn’t fully trust made her start questioning her competence and pushed her to constantly double‑check every decision and commitment. Over the next year, she responded by adding even more structure and effort—late‑night gaming and concerts as her only release—until the constant pressure and self-criticism began to crowd out her enjoyment of basketball, music, and mentoring, and her relationships with roommates and teammates became strained by her short temper and need for control. When she found herself snapping at friends over trivial issues, unable to relax even during yoga, and considering dropping a beloved outreach role because she felt she "couldn’t keep up," an academic advisor who noticed her change in demeanor urged her to see campus mental health services, where she presented for psychiatric evaluation.
patient.chief_complaint: “I’m on edge all the time and I get annoyed over the smallest things, and it’s starting to mess up my relationships.”

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: Most nights I just lie there replaying lab mistakes and to‑do lists for hours, and even when I finally crash after scrolling or gaming way too late, I wake up exhausted like I didn’t really sleep at all and my brain is already racing again before my alarm goes off.

S056.name: Excessive_Anxiety_Worry
S056.description: Excessive anxiety and worry (expectant apprehension) occurring persistently about a number of events or activities.
S056.manifestation: It feels like my brain is constantly running simulations of everything that could go wrong—grades tanking, messing up an experiment, saying something dumb in a meeting, disappointing my profs or my outreach kids—so even when I’m just walking to class or in the shower I’m mentally catastrophizing every little thing.

S057.name: Uncontrollable_Worry
S057.description: The subjective experience of finding it difficult to stop or control the worry.
S057.manifestation: Once the ‘what ifs’ start—like, what if this data is wrong, what if I don’t get an internship, what if everyone realizes I’m faking it—I can’t shut them off no matter how much I tell myself to stop, and they just snowball into these worst‑case scenarios until I’m completely spun out and can’t focus on anything else.

S058.name: Restlessness_Tension
S058.description: Restlessness, or feeling keyed up or on edge.
S058.manifestation: I feel wired and on edge pretty much all the time, like I’ve had five energy drinks, so I’m constantly bouncing my leg, clenching my jaw, checking my email or Canvas, and I literally can’t relax even in yoga because my body won’t stop buzzing.

S060.name: Irritability
S060.description: A state of reacting sensitively or sharply to minor stimuli.
S060.manifestation: I snap over the tiniest things now—like my roommate leaving a mug in the sink or a teammate being five minutes late—and I hear myself being sharp and impatient but it’s like my fuse is so short that I can’t stop it in the moment.
